matutinum.hymn.label: Hymn
matutinum.hymn.title: Verbum supérnum pródiens
matutinum.hymn.lat:
Verbum supérnum pródiens,
a Patre olim éxiens,
qui natus orbi súbvenis,
labénte mundi véspere. Illúmina nunc péctora,
tuóque amóre cóncrema;
audíto ut præcónio
sint pulsa tandem lúbrica. Judéxque cum post áderis
rimári facta péctorum,
reddens vicem pro ábditis,
justísque regnum pro bonis. Non demum artémur malis
pro qualitáte críminis,
sed cum beátis cómpotes
simus perénnes cǽlites. Laus, honor, virtus, glória
Deo Patri cum Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
in sæculórum sǽcula. Amen.
matutinum.hymn.eng:
The heavenly Word proceeding forth,
yet leaving not the Father's side,
and going to His work on earth,
had reached at length life's eventide. Enlighten now each heart of ours,
and set them all on fire with Thee;
that, hearing Thy salvation's call,
our wavering steps from sin be free. When Thou as Judge shalt come again
to search the secrets of each heart,
repaying deeds that lie concealed,
and crowning just ones for their part. Let us not then be held by ills
proportioned to our sinful ways,
but with the blessed may we share
the endless joys of heavenly days. All praise and honour, power and might,
to God the Father and the Son,
together with the Paraclete,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymn
laudes.hymn.title: Vox clara ecce íntonat
laudes.hymn.lat:
Vox clara ecce íntonat,
obscúra quæque íncrepat;
pelántur emínus sómnia:
ab ǽthre Christus prómicat. Mens jam resúrgat tórpida,
quæ sorde exstat sáucia;
sidus refúlget jam novum,
ut tollat omne nóxium. En Agnus ad nos míttitur
laxáre gratis débitum;
omnes simul cum lácrimis
precémur indulgéntiam. Ut, cum secúndo fúlserit,
metuénda cunctis júdicis,
non pro reátu púniat,
sed nos pius tunc prótegat. Laus, honor, virtus, glória
Deo Patri cum Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
in sæculórum sǽcula. Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
Hark! a clear voice from heaven sounds,
rebuking all that darkness shrouds;
let troubled dreams be cast afar:
from heaven Christ shines, the Morning Star. Let torpid minds awake anew,
by sinful wounds laid low and few;
a new star gleams upon our sight
to take away each harmful blight. Behold, the Lamb to us is sent
to pardon every debt we owe;
together let us all with tears
implore His mercy here below. So when He comes in glory bright,
the Judge whom every soul must fear,
He shall not punish us for sin,
but lovingly shall shield us here. All praise and honour, power and might,
to God the Father and the Son,
together with the Paraclete,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymn
vesperae.hymn.title: Cónditor alme síderum
vesperae.hymn.lat:
Cónditor alme síderum,
ætérna lux credéntium,
Christe, Redémptor ómnium,
exáudi preces súpplicum. Qui cóndolens intéritu
mortis períre sǽculum,
salvásti mundum lánguidum,
donans reis remédium. Vergénte mundi véspere,
uti sponsus de thálamo,
egréssus honestíssima
Vírginis matris cláusula. Cujus forti poténtiæ
genu curvántur ómnia;
cæléstia, terréstria,
nutu faténtur súbdita. Te, Sancte, fide quǽsumus,
ventúre Judex sǽculi,
consérva nos in témpore
hostis a telo pérfidi. Laus, honor, virtus, glória
Deo Patri cum Fílio,
Sancto simul Paráclito,
in sæculórum sǽcula. Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
Creator of the starry height,
Thy people's everlasting light,
O Christ, Redeemer of us all,
we pray Thee, hear us when we call. Thou, grieving that the ancient curse
should doom to death a universe,
hast found the healing, full of grace,
to cure and save our ruined race. Thou cam'st, the Bridegroom of the bride,
as drew the world to eventide;
proceeding from a virgin shrine,
the spotless Victim all divine. At whose dread Name, majestic now,
all knees must bend, all hearts must bow;
all things celestial Thee shall own,
and things terrestrial, Lord, alone. O Thou, whose coming is with dread
to judge the living and the dead,
preserve us, while we dwell below,
from every insult of the foe. All praise and honour, power and might,
to God the Father and the Son,
together with the Paraclete,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

prima.hymn.label: Hymn
prima.hymn.title: Iam lucis orto sídere
prima.hymn.lat:
Jam lucis orto sídere,
Deum precémur súpplices,
ut in diúrnis áctibus
nos servet a nocéntibus. Linguam refrénans témperet,
ne litis horror ínsonet;
visum fovéndo cóntegat,
ne vanitátes háuriat. Sint pura cordis íntima,
absístat et vecórdia;
carnis terat supérbiam
potus cibíque párcitas. Ut cum dies abscésserit,
noctémque sors redúxerit,
mundi per abstinéntiam
ipsi canámus glóriam. Jesu, tibi sit glória,
qui natus es de Vírgine,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
prima.hymn.eng:
Now in the sun's new dawning ray,
lowly of heart we Thee implore:
that in our every deed this day
Thou keep us free from evil's power. May He our tongues in order hold,
that discord's horror sound not here;
and guard our eyes from sights untold,
that vanities may not appear. O may the inmost heart be pure,
and folly's grasp be far removed;
let abstinence in food endure,
that pride of flesh be reproved. So when the daylight fades away,
and night in turn again draws near,
through abstinence from worldly sway
we sing His glory without fear. All praise, O Jesu, be to Thee,
whom Virgin-born the world adores,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

tertia.hymn.label: Hymn
tertia.hymn.title: Nunc, Sancte, nobis Spíritus
tertia.hymn.lat:
Nunc, Sancte, nobis Spíritus,
unum Patri cum Fílio,
dignáre promptus íngeri
nostro refúsus péctori. Os, lingua, mens, sensus, vigor,
confessiónem pérsonent;
flamméscat igne cáritas,
accéndat ardor próximos. Jesu, tibi sit glória,
qui natus es de Vírgine,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
tertia.hymn.eng:
Come, Holy Ghost, who ever One
reignest with Father and with Son,
it is the hour, our souls possess
with Thy full flood of holiness. Let mouth and tongue, mind, strength, and will,
sound forth our witness to Thy name;
and charity's devouring flame
set all our being in a glow. All praise, O Jesu, be to Thee,
whom Virgin-born the world adores,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

sexta.hymn.label: Hymn
sexta.hymn.title: Rector potens, verax Deus
sexta.hymn.lat:
Rector potens, verax Deus,
qui témperas rerum vices,
splendóre mane illúminas,
et ígnibus merídiem. Exstíngue flammas lítium,
aufer calórem nóxium,
confer salútem córporum,
verámque pacem córdium. Jesu, tibi sit glória,
qui natus es de Vírgine,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
sexta.hymn.eng:
O God of truth, O Lord of might,
who orderest time and change aright,
who sendest the early morning ray,
and lightest with splendour all the day. Extinguish Thou each sinful fire,
and banish every ill desire;
and while Thou keepest the body whole,
shed forth Thy peace upon the soul. All praise, O Jesu, be to Thee,
whom Virgin-born the world adores,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

nona.hymn.label: Hymn
nona.hymn.title: Rerum Deus tenax vigor
nona.hymn.lat:
Rerum Deus tenax vigor,
immótus in te pérmanens,
lucis diúrnæ témpora
succéssibus detérminans. Largíre clarum véspere,
quo vita nusquam décidat,
sed prǽmium mortis sacræ
perénnis instet glória. Jesu, tibi sit glória,
qui natus es de Vírgine,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
nona.hymn.eng:
O strength and stay upholding all creation,
who ever dost Thyself unmoved abide,
yet day by day the light in due gradation
from hour to hour through all its changes guide. Grant to life's day a calm unclouded ending,
an eve untouched by shadows of decay,
the brightness of a holy deathbed blending
with dawning glories of th'eternal day. All praise, O Jesu, be to Thee,
whom Virgin-born the world adores,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

matutinum.hymn.label: Hymn
matutinum.hymn.title: Ex more docti mýstico
matutinum.hymn.lat:
Ex more docti mýstico
servémus hoc jejúnium,
deno diérum círculo
ducto quater notíssimo. Lex et prophétæ prímitus
hoc prætulérunt, póstmodum
Christus sacrávit, ómnium
Rex atque factor témporum. Utámur ergo párcius
verbis, cibis et pótibus,
somno, jocis, et árctius
perstémus in custódia. Vitémus autem nóxia,
quæ súbruunt mentes vagas;
nullúmque demus cállidi
hostis locum tyránnidi. Flectámus iram víndicem,
plorémus ante Júdicem,
clamémus ore súpplici,
dicámus omnes cérnui: Nostris malis offéndimus
tuam, Deus, cleméntiam;
effúnde nobis désuper,
remíssor, indulgéntiam. Meménto quod sumus tui,
licet cadúci, plásmatis;
ne des honórem nóminis
tui, precámur, álteri. Laxa malum quod fécimus,
auge bonum quod póscimus;
placére quo tandem tibi
possímus hic et pérpetim. Præsta, beáta Trínitas,
concéde, simplex Únitas,
ut fructuósa sint tuis
jejuniórum múnera. Amen.
matutinum.hymn.eng:
Once more the solemn season calls
a holy fast for us to keep;
and faithful to the sacred rite
the forty days of Lent we greet. The law and prophets hallowed it
in former times, and Christ our Lord
Himself hath consecrated it,
the King and Maker of all worlds. More sparing therefore let us use
our words, our food, our drink, our sleep,
our mirth; and closer let us keep
the watches of our outward sense. Let us avoid the harmful things
that undermine our wandering minds;
nor give our cunning enemy
a foothold for his tyranny. Let us bend low before the Judge
and weep before Him earnestly,
and cry aloud with suppliant voice,
and prostrate say with one accord: By our offences we have sinned
against Thy mercy, Lord our God;
pour down upon us from on high,
O pardoning One, Thy clemency. Remember that we are Thy work,
though frail and fallen creatures still;
we pray Thee, give not to another
the honour of Thy holy Name. Forgive the evil we have done,
increase the good for which we pray;
that we at last may please Thee well
both here and in eternity. Grant this, O blessed Trinity,
vouchsafe it, Unity supreme,
that this our fast may fruitful be
and bring Thy servants their reward. Amen.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymn
laudes.hymn.title: Iam Christe sol iustítiæ
laudes.hymn.lat:
Iam Christe, sol iustítiæ,
mentis diéscant ténebræ,
virtútum ut lux rédeat,
terris diem cum réparas. Dans tempus acceptábile,
da, fons bonitátis, da,
ut fructuósa sint tuis
jejuniórum múnera. Quo mente fracta lánguidis
sensus vigórem cólligant;
quo carne pressa céteris
detur sálubre gáudium. Concéde nostrum cónteri
corpus per abstinéntiam;
culpæ ut relínquant pábulum
jejúna corda críminum. Præsta, beáta Trínitas,
concéde, simplex Únitas,
ut fructuósa sint tuis
jejuniórum múnera. Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
O Christ, Thou Sun of justice bright,
let darkness leave our troubled minds,
that virtue's light return once more
as Thou restorest day to earth. Grant us this season of Thy grace,
O fount of goodness, grant, we pray,
that fruitful for Thy faithful ones
may be the gifts of fasting days. That minds brought low and languishing
may gather vigour of their sense;
that flesh subdued may freely yield
a salutary joy to all. Grant that our bodies may be crushed
through temperance and abstinence;
that hearts, from guilty feasting freed,
may starve the nourishment of sin. Grant this, O blessed Trinity,
vouchsafe it, Unity supreme,
that this our fast may fruitful be
and bring Thy servants their reward. Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymn
vesperae.hymn.title: Audi benígne Cónditor
vesperae.hymn.lat:
Audi benígne Cónditor
nostras preces cum flétibus
in hoc sacro jejúnio
fusas quadragenário. Scrutátor alme córdium,
infírma tu scis vírium;
ad te revérsis éxhibe
remissiónis grátiam. Multum quidem peccávimus,
sed parce confiténtibus;
ad nóminis laudem tui
confer medélam lánguidis. Sic corpus extra cónteri
dona per abstinéntiam,
jejúnet ut mens sóbria
a labe prorsus críminum. Præsta, beáta Trínitas,
concéde, simplex Únitas,
ut fructuósa sint tuis
jejuniórum múnera. Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
O kind Creator, bow Thine ear
to mark the cry of fervent prayer,
in this our solemn fasting time
of forty days from sin set free. O searcher of the hearts of men,
Thou knowest well our weakness still;
to us who turn to Thee again
pour forth the grace of pardon's thrill. Full oft indeed have we transgressed,
yet spare us, Lord, who now confess;
and for the glory of Thy Name,
bestow upon our sick souls' rest. Grant that the flesh may be subdued
by gift of outward abstinence,
that so the sober mind may fast
from every stain of sinfulness. Grant this, O blessed Trinity,
vouchsafe it, Unity supreme,
that this our fast may fruitful be
and bring Thy servants their reward. Amen.

completorium.hymn.label: Hymn
completorium.hymn.title: Te lucis ante términum
completorium.hymn.lat:
Te lucis ante términum,
rerum Creátor, póscimus,
ut pro tua cleméntia
sis præsul et custódia. Procul recédant sómnia,
et nóctium phantásmata;
hostémque nostrum cómprime,
ne polluántur córpora. Præsta, beáta Trínitas,
concéde, simplex Únitas,
ut fructuósa sint tuis
jejuniórum múnera. Amen.
completorium.hymn.eng:
To Thee before the close of day,
Creator of the world, we pray:
that with Thy wonted favour Thou
wouldst be our guard and keeper now. From all ill dreams defend our sight,
from fears and terrors of the night;
withhold from us our ghostly foe,
that spot of sin we may not know. Grant this, O blessed Trinity,
vouchsafe it, Unity supreme,
that this our fast may fruitful be
and bring Thy servants their reward. Amen.

matutinum.hymn.label: Hymn
matutinum.hymn.title: Pange lingua gloriósi prǽlium certáminis
matutinum.hymn.lat:
Pange lingua gloriósi
prǽlium certáminis,
et super Crucis trophǽo
dic triúmphum nóbilem,
quáliter Redémptor orbis
immolátus vícerit. De paréntis protoplásti
fraude Factor cóndolens,
quando pomi noxiális
morte morsu córruit,
ipse lignum tunc notávit,
damna ligni ut sólveret. Hoc opus nostræ salútis
ordo depopóscerat,
multifórmis proditóris
ars ut artem fálleret,
et medélam ferret inde,
hostis unde lǽserat. Quando venit ergo sacri
plenitúdo témporis,
missus est ab arce Patris
Natus, orbis Cónditor,
atque ventre virgináli
caro factus pródiit. Vagit infans inter arcta
cónditus præsépia,
membra pannis involúta
Virgo Mater álligat,
et pedes manúsque, crura
stricta cingit fáscia. Lustra sex qui jam perégit,
tempus implens córporis,
se volénte, natus ad hoc,
passióni déditus,
Agnus in Crucis levátur
immolándus stípite. Hic acétum, fel, arúndo,
sputa, clavi, láncea;
mite corpus perforátur,
sanguis, unda prófluit;
terra, pontus, astra, mundus
quo lavántur flúmine. Crux fidélis, inter omnes
arbor una nóbilis:
nulla talem silva profert,
flore, germine, fólio:
dulce lignum, dulces clavos,
dulce pondus sústinens. Flecte ramos, arbor alta,
tensa laxa víscera,
et rigor lentéscat ille
quem dedit natívitas,
ut supérni membra Regis
miti tendas stípite. Sola digna tu fuísti
ferre sǽcli prétium,
atque portum præparáre
nauta mundo náufrago,
quam sacer cruor perúnxit
fusus Agni córpore. Glória et honor Deo
usquequáque altíssimo,
una Patri Filióque,
inclyto Paráclito,
cui laus est et potéstas
per ætérna sǽcula. Amen.
matutinum.hymn.eng:
Sing, my tongue, the Saviour's glory,
of His Flesh the mystery sing;
of the Blood, all price exceeding,
shed by our immortal King,
destined, for the world's redemption,
from a noble womb to spring. Of a pure and spotless Virgin
born for us on earth below,
He, as Man, with man conversing,
stayed, the seeds of truth to sow;
then He closed in solemn order
wondrously His life of woe. This the plan of our salvation,
ordered by eternal will,
that the cunning of the traitor
should be foiled by greater skill,
and the healing should be given
whence the foe had wrought the ill. When at length the fullness cometh
of the sacred time decreed,
He is sent, the world's Creator,
from the Father's throne on high,
and in Virgin's womb enfleshed
comes to us in human guise. Lo! He lies, an Infant weeping,
in the narrow manger pressed,
and His limbs the Virgin Mother
wraps in swaddling-bands of rest,
and with tender hands she bindeth
feet and hands and legs full fast. Thirty years among us dwelling,
now His destined time fulfilled,
born for this, He meets His Passion,
giving Himself to be killed;
on the Cross the Lamb is lifted,
where His Blood shall all be spilled. Vinegar and gall and reed here,
spittings, nails, and piercing spear;
lo, the gentle Body rended,
Blood and water flowing clear;
earth and sea and stars and heaven
washed within that saving mere. Faithful Cross, above all other,
one and only noble tree:
none in foliage, none in blossom,
none in fruit thy peer may be;
sweetest wood and sweetest iron,
sweetest weight is hung on thee. Bend thy boughs, O tree of glory,
thy relaxing sinews bend;
for a while the ancient rigour
that thy birth bestowed, suspend,
and the King of heavenly beauty
on thy bosom gently tend. Thou alone wast counted worthy
this world's ransom to sustain,
that a shipwrecked race for ever
should a port of refuge gain,
with the sacred Blood anointed
of the Lamb for sinners slain. Glory and honour to God
the most high for evermore,
one to the Father and the Son
and glorious Paraclete,
to whom be praise and power
through everlasting ages. Amen.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymn
laudes.hymn.title: Lustris sex qui iam peráctis
laudes.hymn.lat:
Lustris sex qui iam peráctis,
tempus implens córporis,
se volénte, natus ad hoc,
passióni déditus,
Agnus in Crucis levátur
immolándus stípite. Hic acétum, fel, arúndo,
sputa, clavi, láncea;
mite corpus perforátur,
sanguis, unda prófluit;
terra, pontus, astra, mundus
quo lavántur flúmine. Crux fidélis, inter omnes
arbor una nóbilis:
nulla talem silva profert,
flore, germine, fólio:
dulce lignum, dulces clavos,
dulce pondus sústinens. Flecte ramos, arbor alta,
tensa laxa víscera,
et rigor lentéscat ille
quem dedit natívitas,
ut supérni membra Regis
miti tendas stípite. Sola digna tu fuísti
ferre sǽcli prétium,
atque portum præparáre
nauta mundo náufrago,
quam sacer cruor perúnxit
fusus Agni córpore. Glória et honor Deo
usquequáque altíssimo,
una Patri Filióque,
inclyto Paráclito,
cui laus est et potéstas
per ætérna sǽcula. Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
Now the thirty years accomplished
of His time of flesh on earth,
born for this, He meets His Passion,
giving Himself to be killed;
on the Cross the Lamb is lifted,
where His lifeblood shall be spilled. Vinegar and gall and reed here,
spittings, nails, and piercing spear;
lo, the gentle Body rended,
Blood and water flowing clear;
earth and sea and stars and heaven
washed within that saving mere. Faithful Cross, above all other,
one and only noble tree:
none in foliage, none in blossom,
none in fruit thy peer may be;
sweetest wood and sweetest iron,
sweetest weight is hung on thee. Bend thy boughs, O tree of glory,
thy relaxing sinews bend;
for a while the ancient rigour
that thy birth bestowed, suspend,
and the King of heavenly beauty
on thy bosom gently tend. Thou alone wast counted worthy
this world's ransom to sustain,
that a shipwrecked race for ever
should a port of refuge gain,
with the sacred Blood anointed
of the Lamb for sinners slain. Glory and honour to God
the most high for evermore,
one to the Father and the Son
and glorious Paraclete,
to whom be praise and power
through everlasting ages. Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymn
vesperae.hymn.title: Vexílla Regis pródeunt
vesperae.hymn.lat:
Vexílla Regis pródeunt,
fulget Crucis mystérium,
quo carne carnis Cónditor
suspénsus est patíbulo. Quo vulnerátus ínsuper
mucróne diro lánceæ,
ut nos laváret crímine,
manávit unda et sánguine. Impleta sunt quæ cóncinit
David fidéli cármine,
dicens: In natiónibus
regnávit a ligno Deus. Arbor decóra et fúlgida,
ornáta Regis púrpura,
elécta digno stípite
tam sancta membra tángere. Beáta cujus bráchiis
sǽcli pepéndit prétium,
statéra facta córporis,
prædámque tulit tártari. O Crux, ave, spes única,
hoc Passiónis témpore:
auge piis justítiam,
reísque dona véniam. Te, fons salútis, Trínitas,
colláudet omnis spíritus;
quos per Crucis mystérium
salvas, fove per sǽcula. Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
The royal banners forward go,
the Cross shines forth in mystic glow,
where He, the Life, did death endure,
and yet by death did life procure. Where deep for us the spear was dyed,
life's torrent rushing from His side,
to wash us in that precious flood
where mingled Water flowed and Blood. Fulfilled is all that David told
in true prophetic song of old;
amidst the nations, God, saith he,
hath reigned and triumphed from the Tree. O Tree of beauty, Tree of light,
O Tree with royal purple dight,
elect on whose triumphal breast
those holy limbs should find their rest. Blest Tree, whose happy branches bore
the wealth that did the world restore,
the beam that weighed the Body's price
and snatched the spoil from sacrifice. O Cross, our one reliance, hail!
In this our Passion-season frail,
grant to the just increase of grace,
and every sinner's guilt efface. Blest Trinity, salvation's spring,
may every soul Thy praises sing;
to those Thou grantest conquest by
the holy Cross, rewards supply. Amen.

prima.hymn.label: Hymn
prima.hymn.title: Iam lucis orto sídere
prima.hymn.lat:
Jam lucis orto sídere,
Deum precémur súpplices,
ut in diúrnis áctibus
nos servet a nocéntibus. Linguam refrénans témperet,
ne litis horror ínsonet;
visum fovéndo cóntegat,
ne vanitátes háuriat. Sint pura cordis íntima,
absístat et vecórdia;
carnis terat supérbiam
potus cibíque párcitas. Ut cum dies abscésserit,
noctémque sors redúxerit,
mundi per abstinéntiam
ipsi canámus glóriam. Glória tibi, Dómine,
qui passus es pro ímpiis,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
prima.hymn.eng:
Now in the sun's new dawning ray,
lowly of heart we Thee implore:
that in our every deed this day
Thou keep us free from evil's power. May He our tongues in order hold,
that discord's horror sound not here;
and guard our eyes from sights untold,
that vanities may not appear. O may the inmost heart be pure,
and folly's grasp be far removed;
let abstinence in food endure,
that pride of flesh be reproved. So when the daylight fades away,
and night in turn again draws near,
through abstinence from worldly sway
we sing His glory without fear. All glory, Lord, to Thee we pay,
who didst for sinners suffer loss,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

tertia.hymn.label: Hymn
tertia.hymn.title: Nunc, Sancte, nobis Spíritus
tertia.hymn.lat:
Nunc, Sancte, nobis Spíritus,
unum Patri cum Fílio,
dignáre promptus íngeri
nostro refúsus péctori. Os, lingua, mens, sensus, vigor,
confessiónem pérsonent;
flamméscat igne cáritas,
accéndat ardor próximos. Glória tibi, Dómine,
qui passus es pro ímpiis,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
tertia.hymn.eng:
Come, Holy Ghost, who ever One
reignest with Father and with Son,
it is the hour, our souls possess
with Thy full flood of holiness. Let mouth and tongue, mind, strength, and will,
sound forth our witness to Thy name;
and charity's devouring flame
set all our being in a glow. All glory, Lord, to Thee we pay,
who didst for sinners suffer loss,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

sexta.hymn.label: Hymn
sexta.hymn.title: Rector potens, verax Deus
sexta.hymn.lat:
Rector potens, verax Deus,
qui témperas rerum vices,
splendóre mane illúminas,
et ígnibus merídiem. Exstíngue flammas lítium,
aufer calórem nóxium,
confer salútem córporum,
verámque pacem córdium. Glória tibi, Dómine,
qui passus es pro ímpiis,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
sexta.hymn.eng:
O God of truth, O Lord of might,
who orderest time and change aright,
who sendest the early morning ray,
and lightest with splendour all the day. Extinguish Thou each sinful fire,
and banish every ill desire;
and while Thou keepest the body whole,
shed forth Thy peace upon the soul. All glory, Lord, to Thee we pay,
who didst for sinners suffer loss,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

nona.hymn.label: Hymn
nona.hymn.title: Rerum Deus tenax vigor
nona.hymn.lat:
Rerum Deus tenax vigor,
immótus in te pérmanens,
lucis diúrnæ témpora
succéssibus detérminans. Largíre clarum véspere,
quo vita nusquam décidat,
sed prǽmium mortis sacræ
perénnis instet glória. Glória tibi, Dómine,
qui passus es pro ímpiis,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
nona.hymn.eng:
O strength and stay upholding all creation,
who ever dost Thyself unmoved abide,
yet day by day the light in due gradation
from hour to hour through all its changes guide. Grant to life's day a calm unclouded ending,
an eve untouched by shadows of decay,
the brightness of a holy deathbed blending
with dawning glories of th'eternal day. All glory, Lord, to Thee we pay,
who didst for sinners suffer loss,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

completorium.hymn.label: Hymn
completorium.hymn.title: Te lucis ante términum
completorium.hymn.lat:
Te lucis ante términum,
rerum Creátor, póscimus,
ut pro tua cleméntia
sis præsul et custódia. Procul recédant sómnia,
et nóctium phantásmata;
hostémque nostrum cómprime,
ne polluántur córpora. Glória tibi, Dómine,
qui passus es pro ímpiis,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
completorium.hymn.eng:
To Thee before the close of day,
Creator of the world, we pray:
that with Thy wonted favour Thou
wouldst be our guard and keeper now. From all ill dreams defend our sight,
from fears and terrors of the night;
withhold from us our ghostly foe,
that spot of sin we may not know. All glory, Lord, to Thee we pay,
who didst for sinners suffer loss,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

matutinum.hymn.label: Hymn
matutinum.hymn.title: Auróra cælum púrpurat
matutinum.hymn.lat:
Auróra cælum púrpurat,
æther resúltat láudibus,
mundus triúmphans júbilat,
horrens avérnus ínfremit. Rex ille dum fortíssimus
de mortis regno rédiit,
trophǽa sese prótulit,
coram Patre victóriæ. Cujus sepúlcrum plúrimo
custóde signábat lapis,
victor triúmphat et suo
mortem sepúlcro fúnerat. Sat funeri, sat lácrimis,
sat est datum dolóribus;
surréxit exstínctor necis,
clamat corúscans Ángelus. Ut sis perénne méntibus
paschále, Jesu, gáudium,
a morte dira críminum
vitæ renátos líbera. Deo Patri sit glória,
et Fílio, qui a mórtuis
surréxit, ac Paráclito,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
matutinum.hymn.eng:
Dawn purples all the eastern sky,
the air resounds with songs of praise,
the world exults in triumph high,
and shuddering hell in horror sways. The King, all strong and valiant, comes
returning from the realm of death,
His trophies of the victory
He bears before the Father's gaze. His sepulchre was sealed with stone
and guarded well on every side,
yet He, the Victor, triumphs forth
and buries death within His grave. Enough of grief, enough of tears,
enough of sorrow and of pain;
the slayer of death has risen now,
the shining Angel cries again. That Thou mayst be to every mind
our Easter joy eternally,
O Jesu, from the dread of sin
set free the souls reborn to life. To God the Father glory be,
and to the Son, who from the dead
arose, and to the Paraclete,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymn
laudes.hymn.title: Sermóne blando Ángelus
laudes.hymn.lat:
Sermóne blando Ángelus
prǽdixit muliéribus:
In Galilǽa Dóminus
vidéndus est quantócius. Illæ dum pergunt cóncitæ,
Apóstolis hoc dícere,
vidéntes eum vívere,
Christi tenent vestígia. Galilǽæ ad alta móntium
se cónferunt Apóstoli,
Jesúque, voti cómpotes,
almo beántur lúmine. Ut sis perénne méntibus
paschále, Jesu, gáudium,
a morte dira críminum
vitæ renátos líbera. Deo Patri sit glória,
et Fílio, qui a mórtuis
surréxit, ac Paráclito,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
With gentle word the Angel bright
foretold unto the women there:
in Galilee the Lord shall be
seen by you all without delay. While hastening forth with eager speed
to tell the Apostles what he said,
they see the Lord alive once more
and clasp His blessed feet in prayer. To Galilee's high mountain tops
the Apostles make their joyful way,
and there, their longing heart's desire,
they see their Jesu's radiant face. That Thou mayst be to every mind
our Easter joy eternally,
O Jesu, from the dread of sin
set free the souls reborn to life. To God the Father glory be,
and to the Son, who from the dead
arose, and to the Paraclete,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymn
vesperae.hymn.title: Ad régias Agni dapes
vesperae.hymn.lat:
Ad régias Agni dapes,
stolis amícti cándidis,
post tránsitum Maris Rubri,
Christo canámus Príncipi. Divína cujus cáritas
sacrum propínat sánguinem,
almíque membra córporis
amor sacérdos ímmolat. Sparsum cruórem póstibus
vastátor horret Ángelus;
fugítque divísum mare,
mergúntur hostes flúctibus. Jam Pascha nostrum Christus est,
paschális idem víctima,
et pura puris méntibus
sinceritátis ázyma. O vera cæli víctima,
subjécta cui sunt tártara,
solúta mortis víncula,
recépta vitæ prǽmia. Victor subáctis ínferis,
trophǽa Christus éxplicat;
cælóque apérto, súbditum
Regem tenebrárum trahit. Ut sis perénne méntibus
paschále, Jesu, gáudium,
a morte dira críminum
vitæ renátos líbera. Deo Patri sit glória,
et Fílio, qui a mórtuis
surréxit, ac Paráclito,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
At the Lamb's high royal feast,
in robes of white we gather round,
the Red Sea's passage now complete,
we sing to Christ our sovereign Lord. Whose love divine doth freely give
His sacred Blood for us to drink,
and Love, the priest, doth immolate
the members of His blessed frame. The avenging Angel sees the Blood
upon the doorposts sprinkled bright,
the parted sea provides a path,
our enemies beneath it drown. Now Christ Himself our Passover,
the self-same paschal Victim slain,
the unleavened bread of purity
to pure and spotless hearts is giv'n. O true Victim, sent from heaven,
to whom the nether world is bound,
the chains of death are loosed at last,
the prize of life is won once more. The Victor, having crushed the depths,
unfurls His trophies to the sky;
the gates of heaven open wide,
He drags the king of darkness down. That Thou mayst be to every mind
our Easter joy eternally,
O Jesu, from the dread of sin
set free the souls reborn to life. To God the Father glory be,
and to the Son, who from the dead
arose, and to the Paraclete,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

completorium.hymn.label: Hymn
completorium.hymn.title: Te lucis ante términum
completorium.hymn.lat:
Te lucis ante términum,
rerum Creátor, póscimus,
ut pro tua cleméntia
sis præsul et custódia. Procul recédant sómnia,
et nóctium phantásmata;
hostémque nostrum cómprime,
ne polluántur córpora. Jesu, tibi sit glória,
qui surrexísti a mórtuis,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
completorium.hymn.eng:
To Thee before the close of day,
Creator of the world, we pray:
that with Thy wonted favour Thou
wouldst be our guard and keeper now. From all ill dreams defend our sight,
from fears and terrors of the night;
withhold from us our ghostly foe,
that spot of sin we may not know. All praise, O risen Lord, to Thee,
who from the dead didst rise again,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

absístat et vecórdia;
carnis terat supérbiam
potus cibíque párcitas. Ut cum dies abscésserit,
noctémque sors redúxerit,
mundi per abstinéntiam
ipsi canámus glóriam. Deo Patri sit glória,

and guard our eyes from sights untold,
that vanities may not appear. O may the inmost heart be pure,

that pride of flesh be reproved. So when the daylight fades away,

sexta.hymn.title: Rector potens, verax Deus

verámque pacem córdium. Deo Patri sit glória,

and to the Son, who from the dead
arose, and to the Paraclete,

matutinum.hymn.label: Hymn
matutinum.hymn.title: Jesu Redémptor ómnium
matutinum.hymn.lat:
Jesu Redémptor ómnium,
quem lucis ante oríginem
parem patérnæ glóriæ
Pater suprémus édidit. Tu lumen et splendor Patris,
tu spes perénnis ómnium,
inténde quas fundunt preces
tui per orbem sérvuli. Meménto, rerum Cónditor,
nostri quod olim córporis,
sacráta ab alvo Vírginis
nascéndo formam súmpseris. Testátur hoc præsens dies,
currens per anni círculum,
quod solus e sinu Patris
mundi salus advéneris. Hunc astra, tellus, ǽquora,
hunc omne quod cælo subest,
salútis auctórem novæ
novo salútat cántico. Et nos, beáta quos sacri
rigávit unda sánguinis,
natális ob diem tui
hymni tribútum sólvimus. Jesu, tibi sit glória,
qui natus es de Vírgine,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
matutinum.hymn.eng:
Jesu, Redeemer of the world,
whom, ere the earliest dawn of light,
the Father from His bosom sent,
co-equal in His glorious might. Thou brightness of the Father's face,
Thou hope of all who live on earth,
give ear to all who cry to Thee,
Thy servants scattered o'er the world. Remember, Maker of all things,
that Thou didst once our nature take,
born of a Virgin's spotless womb,
and clothed in our poor mortal frame. This present day doth testify,
revolving in its yearly course,
that from the Father's throne alone
Thou camest for the world's release. Him heaven and earth, Him ocean's deep,
Him all that dwell beneath the sky,
the Author of the new salvation,
with a new song do glorify. And we, whom Thy most sacred Blood
hath washed and cleansed from every stain,
upon Thy birthday offer here
the tribute of our grateful strain. All praise, O Jesu, be to Thee,
whom Virgin-born the world adores,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

laudes.hymn.label: Hymn
laudes.hymn.title: A solis ortus cárdine
laudes.hymn.lat:
A solis ortus cárdine
ad usque terræ límitem,
Christum canámus Príncipem,
natum María Vírgine. Beátus auctor sǽculi
servíle corpus índuit,
ut carne carnem líberans
ne pérderet quos cóndidit. Castæ Paréntis víscera
cæléstis intrat grátia,
venter Puéllæ bájulat
secréta quæ non nóverat. Domus pudíci péctoris
templum repénte fit Dei;
intácta nésciens virum
concépit alvo Fílium. Enítitur puérpera
quem Gábriel prǽdíxerat,
quem ventre Matris géstiens
Baptísta clausum sénserat. Fœno jacére pértulit,
præsépe non abhórruit,
et lacte módico pastus est
per quem nec ales ésurit. Gaudet chorus cæléstium
et Ángeli canunt Deo,
palámque fit pastóribus
Pastor, Creátor ómnium. Jesu, tibi sit glória,
qui natus es de Vírgine,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
laudes.hymn.eng:
From lands that see the sun arise
to earth's remotest boundaries,
the Virgin-born we sing to praise,
the Christ, the Prince of endless days. The world's great Author, rich in grace,
a servant's form did not disdain,
that, flesh by flesh from sin set free,
He might save those His hands had framed. Within a spotless Mother's breast
the grace of heaven found its nest,
a maiden's womb in secret bore
a mystery unknown before. The mansion of the modest heart
becomes a temple, set apart;
a Virgin, knowing not a man,
conceived a Son by heaven's plan. The noble Mother brought to birth
Him Gabriel's promise told to earth,
whom John, while in his mother's womb,
had leapt with joy to greet and own. He bore to lie upon the hay,
a manger-bed He did not spurn,
and He was fed on drops of milk
by whom the birds are taught to eat. The heavenly choir rejoice and sing,
the Angels chant their God and King;
and Him the shepherds come to see,
the Shepherd, Maker of us all. All praise, O Jesu, be to Thee,
whom Virgin-born the world adores,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

vesperae.hymn.label: Hymn
vesperae.hymn.title: Christe Redémptor ómnium
vesperae.hymn.lat:
Christe Redémptor ómnium,
ex Patre Patris Únice,
solus ante princípium
natus ineffabíliter. Tu lumen, tu splendor Patris,
tu spes perénnis ómnium,
inténde quas fundunt preces
tui per orbem fámuli. Meménto, salútis Auctor,
quod nostri quondam córporis,
ex illibáta Vírgine
nascéndo, formam súmpseris. Hic præsens testátur dies,
currens per anni círculum,
quod solus a sede Patris
mundi salus advéneris. Hunc cælum, terra, hunc mare,
hunc omne quod in eis est,
auctórem advéntus tui
laudat exsúltans cántico. Nos quoque, qui sancto tuo
redémpti sumus sánguine,
ob diem natális tui
hymnum novum concínimus. Jesu, tibi sit glória,
qui natus es de Vírgine,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
vesperae.hymn.eng:
O Christ, Redeemer of us all,
the Father's only Son alone,
who, ere the worlds began to be,
wast born in ways beyond our thought. Thou art the Father's light and gleam,
the hope of all who live on earth;
give ear unto the prayers we pour
from every corner of the world. Remember, Author of our health,
that once, of Virgin Mother born,
Thou tookest on Thee mortal form
to save the race Thyself hadst made. This present day doth testify,
revolving in its yearly course,
that Thou, from Thy Father's throne alone,
didst come to save a ruined world. Him heaven and earth, Him ocean's deep,
Him all that dwell beneath the sky,
the Author of Thine advent here
with joyful song do magnify. And we as well, whom Thy dear Blood
hath cleansed and ransomed from all sin,
upon Thy birthday sing to Thee
a new and joyful hymn of praise. All praise, O Jesu, be to Thee,
whom Virgin-born the world adores,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

completorium.hymn.label: Hymn
completorium.hymn.title: Te lucis ante términum
completorium.hymn.lat:
Te lucis ante términum,
rerum Creátor, póscimus,
ut pro tua cleméntia
sis præsul et custódia. Procul recédant sómnia,
et nóctium phantásmata;
hostémque nostrum cómprime,
ne polluántur córpora. Jesu, tibi sit glória,
qui natus es de Vírgine,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
completorium.hymn.eng:
To Thee before the close of day,
Creator of the world, we pray:
that with Thy wonted favour Thou
wouldst be our guard and keeper now. From all ill dreams defend our sight,
from fears and terrors of the night;
withhold from us our ghostly foe,
that spot of sin we may not know. All praise, O Jesu, be to Thee,
whom Virgin-born the world adores,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

prima.hymn.label: Hymn
prima.hymn.title: Iam lucis orto sídere
prima.hymn.lat:
Jam lucis orto sídere,
Deum precémur súpplices,
ut in diúrnis áctibus
nos servet a nocéntibus. Linguam refrénans témperet,
ne litis horror ínsonet;
visum fovéndo cóntegat,
ne vanitátes háuriat. Sint pura cordis íntima,
absístat et vecórdia;
carnis terat supérbiam
potus cibíque párcitas. Ut cum dies abscésserit,
noctémque sors redúxerit,
mundi per abstinéntiam
ipsi canámus glóriam. Jesu, tibi sit glória,
qui natus es de Vírgine,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
prima.hymn.eng:
Now in the sun's new dawning ray,
lowly of heart we Thee implore:
that in our every deed this day
Thou keep us free from evil's power. May He our tongues in order hold,
that discord's horror sound not here;
and guard our eyes from sights untold,
that vanities may not appear. O may the inmost heart be pure,
and folly's grasp be far removed;
let abstinence in food endure,
that pride of flesh be reproved. So when the daylight fades away,
and night in turn again draws near,
through abstinence from worldly sway
we sing His glory without fear. All praise, O Jesu, be to Thee,
whom Virgin-born the world adores,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

tertia.hymn.label: Hymn
tertia.hymn.title: Nunc, Sancte, nobis Spíritus
tertia.hymn.lat:
Nunc, Sancte, nobis Spíritus,
unum Patri cum Fílio,
dignáre promptus íngeri
nostro refúsus péctori. Os, lingua, mens, sensus, vigor,
confessiónem pérsonent;
flamméscat igne cáritas,
accéndat ardor próximos. Jesu, tibi sit glória,
qui natus es de Vírgine,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
tertia.hymn.eng:
Come, Holy Ghost, who ever One
reignest with Father and with Son,
it is the hour, our souls possess
with Thy full flood of holiness. Let mouth and tongue, mind, strength, and will,
sound forth our witness to Thy name;
and charity's devouring flame
set all our being in a glow. All praise, O Jesu, be to Thee,
whom Virgin-born the world adores,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

sexta.hymn.label: Hymn
sexta.hymn.title: Rector potens, verax Deus
sexta.hymn.lat:
Rector potens, verax Deus,
qui témperas rerum vices,
splendóre mane illúminas,
et ígnibus merídiem. Exstíngue flammas lítium,
aufer calórem nóxium,
confer salútem córporum,
verámque pacem córdium. Jesu, tibi sit glória,
qui natus es de Vírgine,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
sexta.hymn.eng:
O God of truth, O Lord of might,
who orderest time and change aright,
who sendest the early morning ray,
and lightest with splendour all the day. Extinguish Thou each sinful fire,
and banish every ill desire;
and while Thou keepest the body whole,
shed forth Thy peace upon the soul. All praise, O Jesu, be to Thee,
whom Virgin-born the world adores,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.

nona.hymn.label: Hymn
nona.hymn.title: Rerum Deus tenax vigor
nona.hymn.lat:
Rerum Deus tenax vigor,
immótus in te pérmanens,
lucis diúrnæ témpora
succéssibus detérminans. Largíre clarum véspere,
quo vita nusquam décidat,
sed prǽmium mortis sacræ
perénnis instet glória. Jesu, tibi sit glória,
qui natus es de Vírgine,
cum Patre et almo Spíritu,
in sempitérna sǽcula. Amen.
nona.hymn.eng:
O strength and stay upholding all creation,
who ever dost Thyself unmoved abide,
yet day by day the light in due gradation
from hour to hour through all its changes guide. Grant to life's day a calm unclouded ending,
an eve untouched by shadows of decay,
the brightness of a holy deathbed blending
with dawning glories of th'eternal day. All praise, O Jesu, be to Thee,
whom Virgin-born the world adores,
with Father and with Holy Ghost,
through everlasting ages. Amen.
